tools.name: search_devices
tools.title: Search devices
tools.description: Find device types in the FRC device catalog by name, vendor, part number or slug. Gives each slug (for add_device), its size and its ports: port name, layer (power, can, network, air), + or − polarity for single-conductor power ports, and label.

query.description: Words to look for, for example "spark flex", "pdh", "limelight".

type.description: Only this type: controllers, power, motor-controllers, motors, communication, sensors, vision, pneumatics, lights, driver-station.

include_legacy.description: Also show devices that are not sold now.

tools.name: get_device_type
tools.title: Get a device type
tools.description: One device type from the catalog with its description and all its ports.

tools.name: get_diagram
tools.title: Get the diagram
tools.description: The current diagram, with the changes the person made in the browser: devices (id, type, name, position, box in mm, CAN ID and bus, IP, notes, fields, label side) and wires (layer, ends, fuse, gauge, note). Call it before you edit after the person has had the diagram open.

tools.name: new_diagram
tools.title: New diagram
tools.description: Make a new, empty diagram file and work on it. It does not overwrite a file that exists (use open_diagram).

path.description: The file, for example "~/robot/robot.paradox.json". A relative path is from the folder the server started in.

tools.name: open_diagram
tools.title: Open a diagram
tools.description: Open a .paradox.json file (from the app's Export → JSON, or one made here) and work on it.

path.description: The file. A relative path is from the folder the server started in.

tools.name: open_in_browser
tools.title: Open in the browser
tools.description: Give the person the live link and open it in their browser. In the browser they see each change you make at once, and you see theirs with get_diagram. The link works only on this computer, while this server runs.

tools.name: edit
tools.title: Edit the diagram
tools.description: Change the diagram with a list of operations, run in order: add_device, update_device, remove, connect, update_wire, disconnect, place, row, column, align, rotate, label_side, set_label_hidden, set_title. A later operation can use an id that an earlier one made. If one operation fails, nothing changes and the error says which one and why. Ports are written <device-id>.<port>, for example pdh.ch4.

on_label.description: Show "label value" in the device label on the diagram

y.description: Exact y of the device in mm (with x).

left_of.description: Put the device to the left of this device id.

align.description: Line up with the other device: start (left or top), center (default) or end.

place.description: Exact x and y, or one of right_of / left_of / above / below.

tools.name: auto_layout
tools.title: Arrange automatically
tools.description: Arrange the devices from the way they connect: controller and network devices in a row at the top, motor controllers in columns in CAN chain order with their motors beside them, pneumatics to the right, power devices in a row at the bottom (battery, breaker, PDH). Use it once for a first layout, then render and fix details with edit (place, row, align).

ids.description: Only these devices (placed to the right of the others). Default: all.

tools.name: render
tools.title: Render a picture
tools.description: A PNG picture of the diagram as it exports (at most 1600 px wide), and its problems. Look at it after a change to find overlaps, crossed wires and labels in the way. Give a layer to see one layer, or a region (mm) to look closer.

layer.description: One layer; devices with no port on it fade. Default: all.

region.description: An area of the diagram in mm (get_diagram gives each device box).

scale.description: 1 to 4, default 2. Lowered to keep the picture 1600 px wide or less.

tools.name: check
tools.title: Check the diagram
tools.description: List the problems: devices that overlap, labels that cover devices, a CAN ID missing or used twice on one bus, devices with no power wire, a power channel that feeds two devices, unknown device types.

tools.name: undo_last_edit
tools.title: Undo the last edit
tools.description: Reverse your last edit or auto_layout. Changes the person made in the browser since then stay.

instructions:
Paradox Diagram: build an FRC robot wiring diagram with the person, live in their browser.
1. new_diagram (or open_diagram), then open_in_browser so the person can watch and edit.
2. search_devices for each device, then one edit call that adds the devices and connects the ports (power, CAN, network, air).
3. auto_layout for a first arrangement, then render and look at the picture.
4. Fix overlaps and details with edit (place, row, column, align, label_side); check until it reports no problems.
5. The person edits too: call get_diagram before each edit, and never undo their changes.
